aggregate.interpretation: All three videos finish and are materially faster than the user-attributed submission-7 videos, but most obstacle encounters still show a local post-pass slowdown. This supports a localized obstacle-curve braking hypothesis rather than a global speed or braking change.

method.obstacle_detection: HSV orange connected components constrained to plausible circular obstacle area
method.speed_proxy: median Lucas-Kanade optical flow of the background after subtracting camera motion
method.windows: ten frames from 1.6 to 0.8 race-seconds before the closest approach versus ten frames from 0.08 to 0.88 race-seconds after it

code_corroboration.compound_gate: recognized obstacle with road sweep at least 6.0
code_corroboration.example: At target30 and estimated speed40, base safety brake is0.12 but the curve augmentation raises final brake to0.231.

limitations: The videos expose no physical speed, action, policy-camera, seed, source commit, model hash, package hash or official submission receipt.
Optical flow is a relative video speed proxy, not physical telemetry; camera transitions, compression, curvature and launch acceleration can perturb individual ratios.
Screen-center distance is not vehicle-body clearance and does not prove safety margin.
Submission7 and submission11 appear to use the same evaluation layouts, but intermediate changes mean their time difference cannot be attributed to one code factor.
The current compound sweep gate cannot be reconstructed exactly from the rendered replay video.
The evidence motivates a candidate change but cannot validate its closed-loop trajectory behavior.
